purpose: Compare actual photo organs and attribution for eight sparse learner plants, focused on native Central Texas ID and useful exotic weed differentiation.

species.desired_view: Opposite nettle-like leaves with teeth and green clustered axillary flower spikes
Minute white boraginaceous flowers, coiled scorpioid flower arrangement, bristly leaf/stem hairs and nutlets
Leafless orchid stem, flower lip, orchid column and swollen underground coral-like rhizome (only if photographed without disturbance)
Filiform finely divided leaves, compound umbels and ribbed fruits
Mustard four-petaled yellow flowers, finely dissected leaf, developing slender siliques
Burr arrangement and spine structure, flowering grass stem, leaf blade and ligule
Yellow flowerhead side, spiny phyllary appendages, leaves and winged stems
Johnson grass panicle, spikelets, conspicuous white midrib and ligule, rhizomes

policy: No source name alone proves exact botanical ID
Maintain individual copyright and photographer credit
Do not select missing or merely repetitive organs
